Five things almost every beginner gets wrong, in order of how much they cost you: Programme hopping every fortnight. Chasing soreness instead of progress. Skipping legs then wondering why nothing changes. Adding weight faster than technique holds. Training six days when three would've worked. None of these are effort problems. They're all structure problems.

A plateau is usually a recovery problem wearing a training costume. Before you change the programme: are you eating enough, are you sleeping, have you added weight for eight straight weeks with no back-off, and are you actually logging or just guessing? The answer is rarely a new exercise. It's usually a lighter week.
